_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 53-week trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to Cohort A (50 mg) or Cohort B (80 mg), each cohort further randomized 2:1 to olezarsen or matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with genetically confirmed familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) and fasting TG ≥ 880 mg/dL despite very low-fat diet and optimized lipid-lowering therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change in fasting triglycerides from baseline at Month 6 (average of Weeks 23, 25, and 27) for olezarsen 80 mg compared to placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: N=66 randomized (olezarsen 80 mg n=22; olezarsen 50 mg n=21; placebo n=23).
pivotal_trials.result: Olezarsen 80 mg reduced fasting TG at Month 6 by 44.5% relative to placebo (treatment difference -44.5, 95% CI -72.0, -17.0; p=0.0015); the 50 mg comparison was not significant (-21.5, 95% CI -48.2, 5.3; p=0.1153).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and >3% higher than placebo) were injection site reactions (19% vs 9%), decreased platelet count (12% vs 4%), and arthralgia (9% vs 0%). Adverse reactions led to discontinuation in 7% of TRYNGOLZA-treated patients vs 0% placebo, most commonly hypersensitivity reactions.
target_moa: An APOC-III-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) conjugated to triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc3) for hepatocyte delivery; it binds and causes degradation of apoC-III mRNA, reducing serum ApoC-III protein and lowering triglycerides.

rems.type: DRM and DDLO agreed a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits of olezarsen outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application.

summary.text: Olezarsen received fast track designation (January 2023), breakthrough therapy designation (February 2024), orphan drug designation, and priority review for this NDA. Substantial evidence of effectiveness was established via traditional approval using one adequate and well-controlled trial (CS3) plus confirmatory evidence from Trial CS8.

citations.quote: Olezarsen received fast track designation in January 2023, breakthrough therapy designation in February 2024, and priority review for this NDA submission.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) was established with one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation and confirmatory evidence.
The olezarsen FCS program was based on one adequate and well-controlled trial supported by confirmatory evidence generated by Trial CS8, a phase 2 trial in severe and moderate HTG populations.
